answer: Auction identity seats instead of giving them away. Each month the protocol mints 1,000 seats, sold in a Dutch auction starting at 5,000 POA. A seat is non-transferable, bound to one keypair, and expires after 12 months, so a bot farmer must re-win seats every year. At a $600 clearing price, 10,000 sybils cost $6 million, and the fixed supply forces the attacker to wait behind real users for ten months. Newcomers pay once and earn an opal badge of genuine standing. Sybils cross a desert of empty slots while the registry stays an oasis: the nectar of cheap identities dries up at auction.
